u.src: 是一日的傍晚的事。

en: A servant was waiting under the Rashomon Gate for the rain to stop.
u.src: 有一个家将，在罗生门下待着雨住。

en: Under the broad gate, there was no one at all except this man.
u.src: 宽广的门底下，除了这男子以外，再没有别的谁。

en: Only on a large round pillar where the vermilion lacquer had peeled away, a single cricket was perched.
u.src: 只在朱漆剥落的大的圆柱上，停着一匹的蟋蟀。

en: Since this Rashomon stood on Suzaku Avenue, there ought to have been two or three others besides this man, people in ichimegasa hats or soft eboshi caps sheltering from the rain.
u.src: 这罗生门，既然在朱雀大路上，则这男子之外，总还该有两三个避雨的市女笠和揉乌帽子的。

en: Yet apart from this man, there was no one else at all.
u.src: 然而除了这男子，却再没有别的谁。

en: To explain the reason, in the past two or three years Kyoto had been struck one after another by earthquakes, whirlwinds, great fires, famines, and other calamities, so the capital had become especially desolate.
u.src: 要说这缘故，就因为这二三年来，京都是接连的起了地动，旋风，大火，饥馑等等的灾变，所以都中便格外的荒凉了。

en: According to old records, even Buddhist statues and ritual implements were smashed apart,
u.src: 据旧记说，还将佛象和佛具打碎了，

en: and the pieces of wood, still bearing vermilion lacquer and gold or silver leaf, were all piled beside the road and sold as firewood.
u.src: 那些带着丹漆，带着金银箔的木块，都堆在路旁当柴卖。

en: With the whole capital in such a state, naturally no one paid any attention anymore to matters like repairing the Rashomon gate.
u.src: 都中既是这情形，修理罗生门之类的事，自然再没有人过问了。

en: Taking advantage of this desolation, foxes came to live there, and robbers came to live there too;
u.src: 于是趁了这荒凉的好机会，狐狸来住，强盗来住；

en: Before long, a custom even arose of abandoning unclaimed corpses on top of this gate.
u.src: 到后来，且至于生出将无主的死尸弃在这门上的习惯来。

en: So once the sun went down, everyone felt an eerie chill, and no one walked near this gate anymore.
u.src: 于是太阳一落，人们便都觉得阴气，谁也不再在这门的左近走。

ja: どこからともなくこの
en: Instead, many crows had gathered at this place from who knew where.
u.src: 反而许多乌鸦，不知从那里都聚向这地方。

en: In the daytime, one could see countless crows circling, flying and crying around the highest ridge-end ornament.
u.src: 白昼一望，这鸦是不知多少匹的转着圆圈，绕了最高的鸱吻，啼着飞舞。

en: When the sky above the gate turned crimson in the evening light, they looked especially clear, as if sesame seeds had been scattered there.
u.src: 一到这门上的天空被夕照映得通红的时候，这便仿佛撒着胡麻似的，尤其看得分明。

ja: うまでもなく、これらの
en: Needless to say, those crows had come to peck at the flesh of the dead bodies on the gate.
u.src: 不消说，这些乌鸦是因为要喙食那门上的死人的肉而来的了。

en: But today, perhaps because it was too late, not a single one could be seen.
u.src: ——但在今日，或者因为时刻太晚了罢，却一匹也没有见。

en: All that could be seen was old crow droppings clinging in white specks to the stone steps, which were cracking everywhere and sprouting long weeds from their fissures.
u.src: 只见处处将要崩裂的，那裂缝中生出长的野草的石阶上面，老鸦粪粘得点点的发白。

en: The servant set the seat of his washed-out reddish-blue lined robe on the top of the seven steps,
u.src: 家将将那洗旧的红青袄子的臀部，坐在七级阶的最上级，

en: troubled by a large pimple that had appeared on his right cheek, and stared vacantly at the falling rain.
u.src: 恼着那右颊上发出来的一颗大的面疱，惘惘然的看着雨下。

en: The author has already written earlier that the servant was waiting for the rain to stop.
u.src: 著者在先，已写道“家将待着雨住”了。

ja: どうすればよいかという
en: Yet even after the rain stopped, this servant still had no idea what he should do.
u.src: 然而这家将便在雨住之后，却也并没有怎么办的方法。

ja: っていくところである。
en: In ordinary times, he would naturally have gone back to his master's house.
u.src: 若在平时，自然是回到主人的家里去。

en: But his master had dismissed him four or five days before.
u.src: 但从这主人，已经在四五日之前将他遣散了。

en: As was said above, Kyoto at that time had fallen into extreme decline.
u.src: 上文也说过，那时的京都是非常之衰微了；

en: The fact that this servant had now been dismissed by the master he had served for many years was really only a small ripple of that decline.
u.src: 现在这家将从那伺候多年的主人给他遣散，其实也只是这衰微的一个小小的余波。

en: So rather than saying that the servant was waiting for the rain to stop,
u.src: 所以与其说“家将待着雨住”，

en: it would be more accurate to say that the servant caught in the rain had nowhere to go and was at a loss for any solution.
u.src: 还不如说“遇雨的家将，没有可去的地方，正在无法可想”，倒是惬当的。

en: Moreover, today's weather had a strong effect on the Sentimentalisme of this Heian-period servant.
u.src: 况且今日的天色，很影响到这平安朝家将的Sentimentalisme上去。

en: The rain that had begun toward the end of the Hour of the Monkey still showed no sign of stopping by the Hour of the Rooster.
u.src: 从申末下开首的雨，到酉时还没有停止模样。

en: At this moment, the servant first began thinking about what he would do for a living tomorrow.
u.src: 这时候，家将就首先想着那明天的活计怎么办——

ja: どうにかしようという
en: In other words, he was holding a completely uncertain thought, trying to decide what to do about something that could not be dealt with.
u.src: 说起来，便是抱着对于没法办的事，要想怎么办的一种毫无把握的思想，

en: At the same time, without meaning to listen, he found himself hearing the rain that had long been beating down on Suzaku Avenue.
u.src: 一面又并不听而自听着那从先前便打着朱雀大路的雨声。

en: The rain surrounded Rashomon, drizzling in from far away.
u.src: 雨是围住了罗生门，从远处沥沥的打将过来。

en: Dusk made the sky seem low; when one looked up,
u.src: 黄昏使天空低下了；仰面一望，

en: the top of the gate, above its slanting projecting eaves, seemed to hold up the dark, heavy clouds.
u.src: 门顶在斜出的飞甍上，支住了昏沉的云物。

en: Because he had to find some way to deal with what could not be helped, he no longer had time to choose his means.
u.src: 因为要将没法办的事来怎么办，便再没有工夫来拣手段了。

en: If he chose, he would only starve to death in an empty lot or by the roadside;
u.src: 一拣，便只是饿死在空地里或道旁；

en: and then he would merely be carried into this gate and thrown away like a dog.
u.src: 而且便只是搬到这门里来，弃掉了像一只狗。

ja: もさまよって、やっとここへ
en: But if he did not choose, then... The servant's thoughts wandered along the same path many times before finally arriving at this point.
u.src: 但不拣，则——家将的思想，在同一的路线上徘徊了许多回，才终于到了这处所。

ja: つの「ならば」にすぎなかった。
en: Yet even after much time had passed, this one then still ended as nothing more than a then.
u.src: 然而这一个“则”，虽然经过了许多时，结局总还是一个“则”。

en: On the one hand, the servant had certainly accepted the point that he would not choose his means,
u.src: 家将一面固然肯定了不拣手段这一节了，

ja: けれども、その「ならば」に
になるしかない」ということは、
en: but as for the conclusion that naturally followed in order to give that then a place to settle, that he could only become a robber,
u.src: 但对于因为要这“则”有着落，自然而然的接上来的“只能做强盗”这一节，

en: he still did not have enough courage to affirm it outright.
u.src: 却还没有足以积极的肯定的勇气。

en: The servant gave a great sneeze, then lazily stood up.
u.src: 家将打一个大喷嚏，于是懒懒的站了起来。

en: Kyoto in the evening chill was already so cold that one longed for a brazier.
u.src: 晚凉的京都，已经是令人想要火炉一般寒冷。

en: The wind and the dusk blew freely in between the gate pillars.
u.src: 风和黄昏，毫无顾忌的吹进了门柱间。

en: The cricket that had been perched on the vermilion-lacquered pillar had long since gone off somewhere.
u.src: 停在朱漆柱上的蟋蟀，早已跑到不知哪里去了。

en: The retainer hunched his neck, raised the shoulders of his red and blue jacket over a pale yellow undershirt, and looked around the gate.
u.src: 家将缩着颈子，高耸了衬着淡黄小衫的红青袄的肩头，向门的周围看。

en: For if he could find a place where he would not suffer from wind and rain and would not have to worry about being exposed,
u.src: 因为倘寻得一片地，可以没有风雨之患，没有露见之虑，

en: and if he could sleep there peacefully for one night, he meant to spend the night in that place.
u.src: 能够安安稳稳的睡觉一夜的，便想在此度夜的了。

en: Meanwhile, by good fortune, he noticed something leading up to the gate tower,
u.src: 这其间，幸而看见了一道通到门楼上的，

en: a broad ladder, also painted in vermilion lacquer.
u.src: 宽阔的，也是朱漆的梯子。

ja: にすぎないはずだった。
en: Even if there were anyone up there, they would surely be nothing more than dead people.
u.src: 倘在这上面，即使有人，也不过全是死人罢了。

en: The retainer took care that the plain-handled sword at his waist would not slip from its sheath,
u.src: 家将便留心着横在腰间的素柄刀，免得他出了鞘，

en: raised his straw-sandaled foot, and stepped onto the lowest first rung of the ladder.
u.src: 抬起登着草鞋的脚来，踏上这梯子的最下的第一级去。

en: It was a few minutes later.
u.src: 于是是几分时以后的事了。

en: Halfway up the broad staircase leading to the upper story of Rashomon, a man crouched like a cat, held his breath, and peered at what was happening above.
u.src: 在通到罗生门的楼上的，宽阔的梯子的中段，一个男子，猫似的缩了身体，屏了息，窥探楼上的情形。

en: The firelight leaking down from above faintly lit the man's right cheek, the cheek where, among his short whiskers, a red swollen pimple had festered.
u.src: 从楼上漏下来的火光，微微的照着这男人的右颊，就是那短须中间生了一颗红肿化脓的面疱的颊。

en: At first the servant thought that what was above was nothing more than corpses;
u.src: 家将当初想，在上面的只不过是死人；

en: but after climbing two or three steps, he saw that someone had lit a fire, and that the fire was moving this way and that.
u.src: 但走上二三级，却看见有谁明着火，而那火又是这边那边的动弹。

en: This could be understood simply by seeing the murky yellow light reflected and wavering on the coffered ceiling, whose every corner was covered with spiderwebs.
u.src: 这只要看那昏浊的黄色的光，映在角角落落都结满了蛛网的藻井上摇动，也就可以明白了。

en: On this rainy night, up in the upper story of Rashomon, whoever could have lit a fire was certainly no ordinary person.
u.src: 在这阴雨的夜间，在这罗生门的楼上，能明着火的，总不是一个寻常的人。

ja: うようにしてようやくこの
en: The servant, like a lizard, muffled his footsteps and, as though crawling, finally reached the uppermost rung of the steep ladder.
u.src: 家将是蜥蜴似的忍了足音，爬一般的才到了这峻急的梯子的最上的第一级。

en: Pressing his body down as hard as he could and stretching his neck as far as he could, he peered inside the upper story.
u.src: 竭力的帖伏了身子，竭力的伸长了颈子，望到楼里面去。

en: When he looked, the inside of the tower was just as he had heard: several corpses lay scattered about at random. But the reach of the firelight was far narrower than he had expected, and he could not make out how many there were.
u.src: 待看时，楼里面便正如所闻，胡乱的抛着几个死尸，但是火光所到的范围，却比预想的尤其狭，辨不出那些的数目来。

en: In the dimness, he could only tell that there were naked corpses and corpses wearing clothes; naturally, there were both men and women.
u.src: 只在朦胧中，知道是有赤体的死尸和穿衣服的死尸；又自然是男的女的也都有。

en: And those corpses, some with mouths hanging open and some with arms stretched out,
u.src: 而且那些死尸，或者张着嘴或者伸着手，

en: lay strewn every which way across the floorboards, in a state that almost made one doubt they had ever been human.
u.src: 纵横在楼板上的情形，几乎令人要疑心到他也曾为人的事实。

en: Moreover, only the raised parts, such as shoulders and chests, caught the faint light,
u.src: 加之只是肩膀胸脯之类的高起的部分，受着淡淡的光，

en: while the shadows in the lower parts were even darker and blacker, silently mute as though they would remain so forever.
u.src: 而低下的部分的影子却更加暗黑，哑似的永久的默着。

en: The servant came upon the rotting stench of these corpses and instinctively covered his nose.
u.src: 家将逢到这些死尸的腐烂的臭气，不由的掩了鼻子。

en: Yet in the very next instant, that hand forgot all about covering his nose.
u.src: 然而那手，在其次的一刹那间，便忘却了掩住鼻子的事了。

en: For a powerful emotion had almost completely robbed the man of his sense of smell.
u.src: 因为有一种强烈的感情，几乎全夺去了这人的嗅觉了。

en: Only then did the servant's eyes notice a person crouching among the corpses.
u.src: 那家将的眼睛，在这时候，才看见蹲在死尸中的一个人。

en: It was a short, thin, white-haired old woman, dressed in a cypress-bark-colored robe and looking like a monkey.
u.src: 是穿一件桧皮色衣服的，又短又瘦的，白头发的，猴子似的老妪。

en: The old woman held a lit torch in her right hand and stared at the face of one of the corpses.
u.src: 这老妪，右手拿着点火的松明，注视着死尸之一的脸。

en: Judging from the length of the hair, the corpse was probably a woman.
u.src: 从头发的长短看来，那死尸大概是女的。

en: Moved by six parts terror and four parts curiosity, the servant almost forgot to breathe for a time.
u.src: 家将被六分的恐怖和四分的好奇心所动了，几乎暂时忘却了呼吸。

en: To borrow the words of the old chronicler, he felt his hair standing on end.
u.src: 倘借了旧记的记者的话来说，便是觉得“毛戴”起来了。

en: Then the old woman thrust the pine torch into a crack between the floorboards and reached her hand toward the corpse she had already marked out.
u.src: 随后那老妪，将松明插在楼板的缝中，向先前看定的死尸伸下手去，

en: Just as a mother monkey picks lice from her young, she pulled out that long hair strand by strand.
u.src: 正如母猴给猴儿捉虱一般，一根一根的便拔那长头发。

en: The hair, too, seemed to come away easily in her hand.
u.src: 头发也似乎随手的拔了下来。

en: As the hairs were pulled out one by one, the fear in the servant's heart faded little by little.
u.src: 那头发一根一根的拔下来时，家将的心里，恐怖也一点一点的消去了。

en: At the same time, hatred for the old woman gradually began to stir within him.
u.src: 而且同时，对于这老妪的憎恶，也渐渐的发动了。

en: No, to say it was hatred for this old woman may not be quite accurate;
u.src: ——不，说是“对于这老妪”，或者有些语病；

en: rather, his revulsion against all evil was growing stronger little by little.
u.src: 倒不如说，对于一切恶的反感，一点一点的强盛起来了。

en: At that moment, if someone had put to the servant the question he had earlier considered under the gate, whether to starve to death or become a robber,
u.src: 这时候，倘有人向了这家将，提出这人先前在门下面所想的“饿死呢还是做强盗呢”这一个问题来，

en: the servant would probably have chosen starvation without the slightest hesitation.
u.src: 大约这家将是，便毫无留恋，拣了饿死的了。

en: This man's hatred of evil was like the pine torch the old woman had thrust into the crack between the floorboards,
u.src: 这人的恶恶之心，宛如那老妪插在楼板缝中的松明一般，

en: blazing up with such force that it had already reached this intensity.
u.src: 蓬蓬勃勃的燃烧上来，已经到如此。

en: Naturally, the servant did not know why the old woman was pulling hair from the dead.
u.src: 那老妪为什么拔死人的头发，在家将自然是不知道的。

en: So, speaking rationally, he still did not know whether it should be counted as good or evil.
u.src: 所以照“合理的”的说，是善是恶，也还没有知道应该属于那一面。

ja: ることは、それだけでもすでに
en: But to the servant, pulling hair from the dead on top of Rashomon on this rainy night was already an unforgivable evil in itself.
u.src: 但由家将看来，在这阴雨的夜间，在这罗生门的上面，拔取死人的头发，即此便已经是无可宽恕的恶。

en: Needless to say, the servant had of course long since forgotten that he himself had just been thinking of becoming a robber.
u.src: 不消说，自己先前想做强盗的事，在家将自然也早经忘却了。

en: At that, the servant kicked off with both feet and suddenly shot straight up the ladder;
u.src: 于是乎家将两脚一蹬，突然从梯子直蹿上去；

en: Then, with his hand on the plain-hilted sword, he strode up to the old woman.
u.src: 而且手按素柄刀，大踏步走到老妪的面前。

ja: うまでもないことだった。
en: Needless to say, the old woman was startled.
u.src: 老妪的吃惊，是无须说得的。

en: The old woman caught sight of the retainer and sprang straight up, as if she had been released by a crossbow trigger.
u.src: 老妪一瞥见家将，简直像被弩机弹着似的，直跳起来。
“呔，那里走！”

ja: につまずいてよろめき、
en: The servant blocked the old woman as she stumbled over the corpse and tried to escape, and cursed her like this.
u.src: 家将拦住了那老妪绊着死尸踉跄想走的逃路，这样骂。

en: The old woman shoved the servant aside and still tried to run away.
u.src: 老妪冲开了家将，还想奔逃。

en: But the servant would not let her go and pushed her back again and again.
u.src: 家将却又不放伊走，重复推了回来了。

en: For a while, they grappled in silence.
u.src: 暂时之间，默然的叉着。

en: Yet the outcome of the struggle had been clear from the start.
u.src: 然而胜负之数，是早就知道了的。

en: At last the servant seized the old woman's arm and forced her down by twisting it.
u.src: 家将终于抓住了老妪的臂膊，硬将伊捻倒了。

en: It was an arm of nothing but skin and bone, just like the leg of a chicken.
u.src: 是只剩着皮骨，宛然鸡脚一般的臂膊。
“在做什么？
说来！

en: If you will not talk, this is what you will get!
u.src: 不说，便这样！”

en: The servant set the old woman down, suddenly drew his sword from its sheath, and thrust the snowy white gleam of steel before her eyes.
u.src: 家将放下老妪，忽然拔刀出了鞘，将雪白的钢色，塞在伊的眼前。

en: But the old woman did not open her mouth.
u.src: 但老妪不开口。

en: Her hands trembled, her breathing grew labored, and with both eyes wide open, her eyeballs seeming almost ready to fly from their sockets, she stubbornly kept silent as if struck dumb.
u.src: 两手发了抖，呼吸也艰难了，睁圆了两眼，眼珠几乎要飞出窠外来，哑似的执拗的不开口。

en: Seeing this, the servant clearly realized at last that the old woman's life and death were now entirely under the command of his own will.
u.src: 一看这情状，家将才分明的意识到这老妪的生死，已经全属于自己的意志的支配。

en: And that will had already, at some point without his noticing, cooled the fierce hatred he had felt before.
u.src: 而且这意志，将先前那炽烈的憎恶之心，又早在什么叫候冷却了。

en: What remained was only the calm pride and satisfaction felt after accomplishing a task.
u.src: 剩了下来的，只是成就了一件事业时候的，安稳的得意和满足。

en: Then the servant looked down at the old woman and, softening his voice a little, said:
u.src: 于是家将俯视着老妪，略略放软了声音说：

en: I am not an official from the office of the Kebiishi;
u.src: “我并不是检非违使的衙门里的公吏；

en: I am only a traveler who happened to pass under this gate just now.
u.src: 只是刚才走过这闸下面的一个旅人。

en: So I have no business tying you up and taking you away.
u.src: 所以并不要锁你去有什么事。

en: Just tell me what you were doing up here on this gate at this hour.
u.src: 只要在这时候，在这门上，做着什么的事，说给我就是。”

en: The old woman opened her round, staring eyes even wider and fixed them on the servant's face;
u.src: 老妪更张大了圆睁的眼睛，看住了家将的脸；

en: They were red-rimmed eyes, sharp like the eyes of a bird of prey.
u.src: 这看的是红眼眶，鸷鸟一般锐利的眼睛。

en: Then her wrinkled lips, almost joined into one with her nose, began to move as if chewing something.
u.src: 于是那打皱的，几乎和鼻子连成一气的嘴唇，嚼着什么似的动起来了。

en: Her neck was very thin, and the movement of her pointed Adam's apple could be seen.
u.src: 颈子很细，能看见尖的喉节的动弹。

en: At that moment, from that throat came a crow-like voice, panting as it reached the servant's ears:
u.src: 这时从这喉咙里，发出鸦叫似的声音，喘吁吁的传于家将的耳朵里：

en: I am plucking out this hair, plucking it out, to make a wig.
u.src: “拔了这头发呵，拔了这头发呵，去做假发的。”

en: When the retainer heard that the old woman's answer was unexpectedly ordinary, he could not help feeling disappointed;
u.src: 家将一听得这老妪的答话是意外的平常，不觉失了望；

en: And as soon as disappointment came, his earlier hatred and cold contempt entered his heart again at the same time.
u.src: 而且一失望，那先前的憎恶和冷冷的侮蔑，便同时又进了心中了。

en: From his expression, she too probably understood it.
u.src: 他的气色，大约伊也悟得。

en: The old woman still clutched in one hand the long hair she had pulled from the corpse, and, making a croaking sound like a toad, said these words:
u.src: 老妪一手仍捏着从死尸拔下来的长头发，发出虾蟆叫一样声音，格格的，说了这些话：

en: Of course, pulling hair from the dead is an evil thing, though I truly cannot say how evil.
u.src: “自然的，拔死人的头发，真不知道是怎样的恶事呵。

en: But all these dead people here are people who deserved to have such things done to them.
u.src: 只是，在这里的这些死人，都是，便给这么办，也是活该的人们。

en: Just now, the woman whose hair I was pulling used to cut snakes into four-inch pieces, dry them, call them dried fish, and sell them at the camp of the armed men.
u.src: 现在，我刚才，拔着那头发的女人，是将蛇切成四寸长，晒干了，说是干鱼，到带刀的营里去出卖的。

en: If she had not caught the plague, she would probably still be going out to sell them now.
u.src: 倘使没有遭瘟，现在怕还卖去罢。

en: This person was the same: the dried fish that woman sold was said to taste good, and the armed men bought it as an indispensable side dish.
u.src: 这人也是的，这女人去卖的干鱼，说是口味好，带刀们当作缺不得的菜料买。

en: As for me, I do not think what this woman did was evil.
u.src: 我呢，并不觉得这女人做的事是恶的。

en: If she had not done it, she would have starved, so she did it because she had no choice.
u.src: 不做，便要饿死，没法子才做的罢。

en: In that case, I do not think what I am doing is evil either.
u.src: 那就，我做的事，也不觉得是恶事。

en: This too is something I do because, if I do not, I will starve and have no other way.
u.src: 这也是，不做便要饿死，没法子才做的呵。

ja: このやむをえぬことをよく
en: This woman, who understands very well what it means to have no choice, should surely forgive me too.
u.src: 很明白这没法子的事的这女人，料来也应该宽恕我的。”

en: The old woman had probably said something to that effect.
u.src: 老妪大概说了些这样意思的事。

en: The servant put his sword back into its sheath, kept his left hand on the hilt, and listened coldly to these words;
u.src: 家将收刀进了鞘，左手按着刀柄，冷然的听着这些话；

en: As for his right hand, it was naturally pressed against the large red pimple on his cheek that had filled with pus.
u.src: 至于右手，自然是按着那通红的在颊上化了脓的大颗的面疱。

en: Yet as he listened, a kind of courage began to arise in the servant's heart.
u.src: 然而正听着，家将的心里却生出一种勇气来了。

en: It was precisely the courage this man had lacked earlier beneath the gate.
u.src: 这正是这人先前在门下面所缺的勇气。

en: Moreover, it was courage moving in the exact opposite direction from the courage that had made him leap up into this gate earlier to seize the old woman.
u.src: 而且和先前跳到这门上，来捉老妪的勇气，又完全是向反对方面发动的勇气了。

en: For the servant, whether to starve to death or become a robber had long since ceased to be a question;
u.src: 家将对于或饿死或做强盗的事，不但早无问题；

en: Judging from this man's state of mind at that moment, such a thing as starving to death had already been driven out of his awareness and was almost unthinkable.
u.src: 从这时候的这人的心情说，所谓饿死之类的事，已经逐出在意识之外，几乎是不能想到的了。
“的确，这样么？”

en: After the old woman finished speaking, the retainer said again in a mocking voice, as if pressing her to confirm it.
u.src: 老妪说完话，家将用了嘲弄似的声音，覆核的说。

en: Then he stepped forward, his right hand suddenly leaving that pimple, seized the old woman by the front of her chest, and said through clenched teeth:
u.src: 于是前进一步，右手突然离开那面疱，捉住老妪的前胸，咬牙的说道：

en: Then, even if I take it by force, you probably will not resent me.
u.src: “那么，我便是强剥，也未必怨恨罢。

ja: だって、こうしなければ、
en: I, too, will starve to death if I do not do this.
u.src: 我也是不这么做，便要饿死的了。”

en: The servant quickly stripped the old woman of her clothes.
u.src: 家将迅速的剥下这老妪的衣服来；

en: Then he violently kicked down the old woman who had clung to his leg, knocking her onto the corpses.
u.src: 而将挽住了他的脚的这老妪，猛烈的踢倒在死尸上。

en: It was only five steps to the stairway entrance.
u.src: 到楼梯口，不过是五步。

en: The servant tucked the stripped-off cypress-bark-colored clothing under his arm and, in an instant, went down the steep stairs into the dark night.
u.src: 家将挟着剥下来的桧皮色的衣服，一瞬间便下了峻急的梯子向昏夜里去了。

en: Before long, the old woman, who had seemed for a while to have stopped breathing, struggled her naked body up from among the corpses.
u.src: 暂时气绝似的老妪，从死尸间挣起伊裸露的身子来，是相去不久的事。

en: She let out a rambling, groaning sound,
u.src: 伊吐出唠叨似的呻吟似的声音，

en: using the light of the fire that was still burning, and crawled over to the stairway entrance.
u.src: 借了还在燃烧的火光，爬到楼梯口边去。

en: Then from there she let her short white hair hang upside down and peered beneath the gate.
u.src: 而且从这里倒挂了短的白发，窥向门下面。

en: Outside there was only the pitch-dark night.
u.src: 那外边，只有黑洞洞的昏夜。

en: No one knew the whereabouts of the retainer.
u.src: 家将的踪迹，并没有知道的人。
鲁迅 译
上海商务印书馆
